certificate.title: Anonymize Technical Accounting Memos with AI Completion

course.description: Use AI to remove sensitive client data from technical accounting memos while simultaneously reformatting them to match your firms latest branding guidelines.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in Anonymize Technical Accounting Memos with AI.

lessons.content:
## Gather the Memos You Want to Anonymize

Start by selecting the technical accounting memos you want to turn into shareable examples.

### What to prepare:
1. Select memos that showcase your firm's best work — complex topics, thorough analysis, clean structure
2. Gather them in PDF or Word format for uploading to AI
3. Also grab your firm's **current branding guidelines** — logo usage, fonts, header/footer templates, color scheme, formatting standards

### What makes a good candidate:
- Technical accounting memos (revenue recognition, lease accounting, business combinations, etc.)
- Memos with enough substance to demonstrate expertise
- Older client work where the engagement is fully closed

### Before you start:
- Know what counts as sensitive: client names, deal values, dates, entity names, counterparty names, specific financial figures, addresses, employee names
- Decide if you want to fully anonymize (replace with generic placeholders) or partially anonymize (keep industry context but strip identifiers)
lessons.title: Prepare Your Source Memos

activities.title: Set Up the AI with Dual Instructions

lessons.content:
## Configure AI for Anonymization + Rebranding in One Pass

The power move here is having AI do both jobs at once — strip sensitive data AND reformat to your current brand standards.

### Prompt framework:
> I am going to provide you with a technical accounting memo from a client engagement. I need you to do two things simultaneously:
>
> **1. Anonymize all sensitive information:**
> - Replace client/entity names with generic placeholders (e.g., "Company A", "Target Co")
> - Replace specific dollar amounts with representative figures (e.g., "$X million")
> - Remove or generalize dates (e.g., "Q3 2024" → "the reporting period")
> - Strip counterparty names, addresses, employee names, and deal-specific identifiers
> - Preserve the technical substance and analytical flow
>
> **2. Reformat to our current branding guidelines:**
> [Paste or describe your firm's formatting standards — headers, fonts, section structure, disclaimer language, etc.]
>
> Output: A clean, anonymized version of the memo in our current brand format that I can use as a work product example.

### Pro tip:
If you have a branded Word template, describe its structure to AI (header style, section numbering, font choices). The closer the description, the less cleanup you'll do after.
lessons.title: Set Up the AI with Dual Instructions

activities.title: Upload Memo and Generate Clean Version

lessons.content:
## Feed the Memo and Get Your Anonymized Output

Upload the memo and let AI produce the cleaned, rebranded version.

### Steps:
1. Upload the original memo to your AI tool (ChatGPT, Claude, etc.)
2. Let AI process it with both instructions active
3. Review the output for:
   - **Anonymization completeness** — scan for any client names, dollar amounts, or identifiers that slipped through
   - **Technical accuracy** — make sure the anonymization didn't break the analytical logic or remove context needed to follow the reasoning
   - **Branding compliance** — check headers, section structure, and formatting match your standards
4. If anything was missed, ask AI to do a second pass focusing on the specific issues

### Common gotchas:
- AI sometimes misses names buried in footnotes or cross-references
- Dollar amounts in tables may not get caught on the first pass
- Industry-specific jargon might inadvertently identify the client (e.g., a unique product name)
lessons.title: Upload Memo and Generate Clean Version

lessons.content:
## Do a Final Sweep Before Sharing

The AI output is your 80% draft — the final 20% is a human review to make sure nothing sensitive survived.

### Final review checklist:
1. **Ctrl+F for known sensitive terms** — search the output for any original client names, entity names, or deal identifiers you remember from the source
2. **Read through once as an outsider** — could someone reading this figure out which client this was? If yes, generalize further
3. **Check consistency** — if AI replaced "Acme Corp" with "Company A" in one place but "the Client" elsewhere, standardize it
4. **Verify the branding** — headers, footers, disclaimers, and formatting should match your current template
5. **Save the final version** — export to Word/PDF in your branded template

### Output:
A polished, anonymized technical accounting memo that:
- Contains zero client-identifying information
- Follows your firm's current branding and formatting
- Showcases the quality of your technical work
- Is ready to share with prospects, new hires, or in proposals

### Pro tip:
Build a small library of these over time. Having 5-10 anonymized examples across different technical topics is a powerful business development asset.
